articles.title: Square Enix PlayStation Exclusive Game Now Available for $1.59
articles.summary: A Square Enix PlayStation exclusive game is now available for $1.59 on the PlayStation Store for a limited time. More precisely, until November 21. After this, the 80% discount that creates this price point will expire. The game in question hails from 2014 and was notably a mobile game developed internally at Square Enix by […]
articles.content:
Fresh off the back of releasing one of the best PS5 games last month , Square Enix has made Hitman Go available to PS5, PS4, and PS Vita users for $1.59. There is notably no native PS5 version of the Square Enix game, but it is playable on the current Sony console thanks to backward compatibility with its previous console. Considering the game has been sitting dormant for 10 years, it's unlikely it will get a native PS5 port at this point.

For those unfamiliar with this release, it is a turn-based puzzle game and the debut release from Square Enix Montreal, which would go on to make a handful of other mobile games, but which hasn't put anything out since 2022. And that's because the team has effectively been dissolved. Hitman Go is not just the studio's first game, but the game it is best known for.

A Great Puzzle Game From the Mid 2010s When Hitman Go was released in the 2010s, it earned an 81 on Metacritic and made a large impression for being such a different experience in the stealth series. To this end, it was one of the better mobile games of the decade.

As for the game itself, it is essentially Hitman meets chess. In it, you guide Agent 47, the series' protagonist, through various grid-based levels with characters modelled after miniature figurines.

To date, it has over 3,700 user reviews on the PlayStation Store, with an average rating of 4.33 out of 5 stars, with well over half of the game's reviews giving it a perfect 5/5 stars.

That said, those who pick up the Hitman game shouldn't expect a ton of content out of it. To this end, it is about 5 to 8 hours long, but at $1.59, this is a great ROI, content-wise. Unfortunately, though, the game does not have great replayability, but it does hold up very well in 2026. In fact, it hasn't really aged at all due to the nature of the game.

articles.title: The Nielsen Tide: How SEC Teams Dominate College Football Viewership
articles.summary: Two years ago, college football's mighty Southeastern Conference moved its primary TV contract from CBS to ABC and ESPN. The conference was in search of more national TV coverage of the regular season games played on Saturdays by its 16 teams that include some of the most dominant squads in all of college gridiron: including […]
articles.content:
Two years ago, college football ‘s mighty Southeastern Conference moved its primary TV contract from CBS to ABC and ESPN .

The conference was in search of more national TV coverage of the regular season games played on Saturdays by its 16 teams that include some of the most dominant squads in all of college gridiron: including the University of Alabama, University of Georgia, University of Texas, Louisiana State University, University of Mississippi (aka Ole Miss), Vanderbilt University and Auburn University. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Robert Pattinson to Receive 40th American Cinematheque Award 'Triplets of Belleville' Director Sylvain Chomet Fires Back at AI Accusations Over Dior Film Featuring Robert Pattinson's Voice: ‘Everything Was Drawn by Hand’ (EXCLUSIVE)

Last year, the SEC logged its most-watched football season in history. This year, viewership is on track to meet or exceed last year's mark. And the importance of college football to driving the overall business of linear TV can't be overstated — as evidenced by Fox Sports' recent investment in college games.

The SEC and the teams it encompasses have been dominant forces in college football for nearly a century (the conference was formed in 1932). But the move to ABC/ESPN offered SEC teams significantly more TV windows for all of its teams, from 15 per season at CBS to 40 with ABC/ESPN. And little more than halfway through the 2026 college football season, the data makes it crystal clear that SEC teams are more powerful than ever when it comes to energizing fans and driving TV viewership.

On Nov. 7, the showdown between Alabama and LSU delivered the most-watched game of the 2026 college football season to date with 8.9 million people tuning in for the game that aired in ABC/ESPN's lucrative afternoon window. The Crimson Tide topped LSU 31-13, much the delight of Alabama's passionate fans. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"Our strategic partnership with Disney has been a great success for the SEC, maximizing the reach of our content across broadcast, cable and streaming platforms," said Matt Evans, the SEC's assistant commissioner for network relations. "It has more than doubled the number of football games available to fans on over-the-air television, from 15 under our previous contract with CBS to more than 35 each season on ABC, which has helped drive record-breaking viewership for the SEC."

The SEC has had its own SEC Network channel distributed via ESPN since 2014. That channel has been a welcome vehicle to showcase the wide range of men's and women's sports played by SEC schools, from track and field, softball and volleyball to rowing, swimming and gymnastics. But the ratings delivered by every other sport combined doesn't come close to the audience commanded by football.

In 2025, SEC teams accounted for 14 of college football's 25 most-watched teams, including eight of the top 10. Alabama ranked No. 1 by a comfortable margin with an average of 9 million across regular season and playoff games. Ohio State ranked No. 2 with 8.6 million, followed by SEC teams Georgia (8.3 million), LSU (8 million), Texas (7.7 million) and Ole Miss (6.5 million). This reinforces the SEC's motto "It just means more."

Last season, SEC games overall averaged 5.1 million viewers per game, a gain of 4% over the 2024 season. SEC games drew larger audiences than its three biggest conference rivals: the Big 10 (by a 65% margin), the Atlantic Coast Conference (by 141%) and the Big 12 (269%), according to SEC research. For the 2025 season, SEC games drove some 1.1 billion live viewing hours, compared to 775 million for the Big 10, 486 million for ACC and 424 million for the Big 12.

The SEC data is significant at a time when the College Football Playoff schedule is poised to expand significantly starting with the 2027-28 season in an effort to give more teams a chance to compete for postseason berths. There's no question that winning teams and teams that make playoff berths generate enthusiasm from schools and alumni, especially the devoted football boosters who deliver energy and big-money contributions to support schools and teams.

The SEC's storied history and the track records of its schools give the conference teams a leg up in recruiting top high school players. But in the era when name, image and likeness rights for players has driven eye-popping numbers in collegiate sports, the SEC has an interest in demonstrating the muscle it teams flex on TV. After all, getting exposure on national TV is crucial for players who want to make the leap to the NFL or otherwise capitalize on their college fame after graduation. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The SEC also emphasizes its rich tradition and the spectacle of games that can draw crowds as big as the NFL in some cases. After a few years of disruption and team shake-ups among other college conferences, the SEC is a bastion of stability. It also remains a regionally centered conference as all of its schools are in states that are contiguous, which means that fans can more easily travel to games.

articles.title: There’s A New Harry Potter TV Clip, And Now I’m Even More Excited For John Lithgow As Dumbledore
articles.summary: Dumbledore! Dumbledore! Dumbledore!
articles.content:
"Dumbledore! Dumbledore! Dumbledore!" Is how the new clip to HBO's Harry Potter TV show opens, and you know what? I get it. I've been curious about how John Lithgow would tackle the iconic role, and this latest clip gives me even more confidence that he's a great choice for the role. The debut for this new book to screen adaptation of the Harry Potter series is right around the corner. And while subscribers of HBO and those with an HBO Max subscription still have weeks to wait, the premium cable channel gave us a scene from the series.

The clip opens with the newly sorted first years seated with the rest of their houses and chanting for Dumbledore. Once they're tucking into their feast, Dumbledore and Professor McGonagall have a chat about Harry being sorted into Gryffindor. "The cat that got the cream" is a clever idiom from the headmaster, when taking into account McGonagall's animagus abilities. For such a brief conversation, it really tells us a lot about the headmaster. He's playful and thoughtful all at once.

When Minerva comments on how much Harry looks like his father, Dumbledore's response is:

I love that Dumbledore isn't quick to assume Harry is everything like his father. McGonagall's tone is affectionate of course, but still softly suggests some expectation from the 11-year-old that Dumbledore seems quick to gently shut down. There are so many sides to Albus Dumbledore, and I love how this clip shows Lithgow grasping more than one of them.

articles.title: Big Shonen Jump Hit Confirms It Will End After 6 Years With Next Release
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Shueisha One of the biggest hits to come out of the pages of Shueisha's Weekly Shonen Jump magazine has now revealed it's set to end after six years of serialization with its final chapter coming very soon. It's been a rollercoaster of a year for Shonen Jump as there have been a number of longer running […]
articles.content:
There have been five longer running titles that have come to an end with Shonen Jump through the year thus far , and now Yuto Suzuki's Sakamoto Days has confirmed that it will be coming to an end with the release of its final chapter next week. This will mark a total of six years of serialization within Shonen Jump , and will be an end to one of the longer running series in the magazine of the early 2020s era. So it's time to say goodbye before the end comes.

Sakamoto Days has been circling its end for quite a while now, and that's all going to be set with Chapter 284 coming this Sunday, November 22nd. The final arc of Yuto Suzuki's manga originally began late last year as Taro Sakamoto and the others needed to deal with X and the destruction of the former assassination system . It's been one intense final fight after another, and it all seemed to be wrapping up with its latest chapters. This seemed to be even more the case with Chapter 282 as Sakamoto was able to deal the final blow to X and end the fight once and for all.

Sakamoto Days' penultimate chapter (Chapter 283) then picks up a year after the fight with X , and reveals that Sakamoto has since opened up even more of his convenience stores all over Japan in that time (just like he dreamed he would). Revealing how Japan has basically returned to peace after all that time, Sakamoto and the others have been working hard to maintain it. But as it gears up for its finale, Sakamoto's daughter Hana has been kidnapped and it has sparked one final adventure to go out on.

The end of Sakamoto Days comes just a week after Kenta Shinohara's Witch Watch released its own final chapter after a five year long run . This marks another two of the longer running hits from Shonen Jump coming to an end one after another, and puts one more nail in the coffin of the late 2010s-early 2020s generation of titles. This will also be the sixth series to reach its respective conclusion with the magazine this year after Jujutsu Kaisen Modulo, Hima-ten!, Blue Box and The Elusive Samurai before it.

There are three new titles coming to Shonen Jump through the rest of the month with the first, Jan Is in Danger! , making its own debut this week . That means two replacements are set with Sakamoto Days getting its own replacement soon, and it likely means another title is going to end next week. It's likely going to be a cancellation, however, as nothing else seems ready to end by its own terms right now. But how do you feel about Sakamoto Days ending after six years? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

articles.title: Fans Have BIG Reactions To Robert Pattinson Becoming The New Bond (And Pass The Popcorn)
articles.summary: Denis Villeneuve's Bond was finally revealed, and fans have thoughts.
articles.content:
Generations of moviegoers grew up with the James Bond movies , making it one of the most recognizable (and profitable) franchises in the film industry. Ever since Daniel Craig's Bond run ended with No Time to Die , those fans have been curious on who will take on the mantle of 007 next. Robert Pattinson was just confirmed for the role, and folks are sounding off online about this choice. Pass me the popcorn, cuz they're not holding back.

No Time to Die' s ending killed off Craig's Bond, and fans have spent years taking bets on who would replace him. Now we finally know that Robert Pattinson will have that honor, and there are plenty of folks who are thrilled with this news after his acclaimed roles in projects like The Odyssey , The Drama , and Primetime . Some of those excited responses from social media read:

Robert Pattinson has been an A-list actor since starring in the Twilight movies , and since then he's spent years building a diverse career, both in indie films and major blockbusters like The Batman . There are no franchises quite as huge as James Bond, so this is once again going to put him at the center of the pop culture landscape. Clearly the 40 year-old actor impressed director Denis Villeneuve when working with him on Dune: Part Three (which hits theaters this December).

Given how strongly cinephiles feel about the James Bond franchise, there are also plenty of naysayers who aren't pleased about Robert Pattinson taking on the mantle of 007. Those critics are definitely making their voices known on the casting announcement, with some responses reading:

Clearly the fandom is not in agreement about whether or not Pattinson was the right choice to play 007. There are plenty of folks who are not happy about this choice, and who would prefer to see Henry Cavill as James Bond. The Man of Steel actor has expressed interest in the role for a while now, and even auditioned back when Craig was hired. We'll just have to wait and see if the Mickey 17 actor wins over his naysayers.

articles.title: Bob Odenkirk, Alec Baldwin, Isla Fisher to Headline Tribeca Festival’s 2026 Portugal Edition
articles.summary: Zosia Mamet, Edward Burns, Zach Woods and W. Kamau Bell are also headed to Lisbon for Tribeca Lisboa Festival, which booked ‘Josephine,’ ‘The Incomer’ and ‘Queen at Sea’ into its film lineup.
articles.content:
Tribeca Festival has Bob Odenkirk, Alec Baldwin, Isla Fisher, Zosia Mamet, Edward Burns, Zach Woods and W. Kamau Bell set to headline its spinoff Tribeca Festival Lisboa in Lisbon next month.

Tribeca's third annual Portugal edition, running Dec. 9 to 13, has booked indie talent for film screenings and conversations to complement local stars from Lisbon's creative community as a cross-Atlantic indie film showcase during Hollywood's awards season.

Odenkirk, who, alongside David Cross, brought their documentary Bob and David Climb Machu Picchu to Tribeca in June 2026, will be on hand for a Dec. 11 premiere in Lisbon. Other Tribeca titles tapped include Zach Woods bringing The Accompanist , his feature directorial debut, and Edward Burns on hand for a fest screening of Finnegan's Foursome , which he directed and stars in. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories TV 'American Doctor' Doc Distributor Condemns Gaza Hospital Bombing Death of Dr. Rizk Abu Shaaira Movies Swiss Queer Film Fest Drops Israeli Film After Boycott Threats: "We're Not Sundance, Right?"

Tribeca Lisboa Festival has also booked the Sundance award winners Josephine , starring Mason Reeves, Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan and directed by Beth de Araújo, and director Louis Paxton's The Incomer, along with the Berlinale Silver Bear winner Queen at Sea, from director Lance Hammer and starring Juliette Binoche and Tom Courtenay.

Also headed to Lisbon from Tribeca's 2026 edition in New York City is Here I'm Alive , a neo-realist urban epic directed by Joshua Z. Weinstein; In Memoriam , directed by Rob Burnett and starring Marc Maron, Talia Ryder and Lily Gladstone; and Rachel Rose's The Last Day, a contemporary take on Virginia's Woolf's Mrs. Dalloway classic novel that stars Alicia Vikander, Victoria Pedretti and Wagner Moura. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

“Following a banner year in New York, it's especially meaningful to see the festival's spirit taking root in Lisbon, with audiences who are as curious and passionate about storytelling as we are,” Cara Cusumano, Tribeca Festival director and senior vp of programming, said of the indie titles she curated for Tribeca Lisboa Festival 2026. “Our program brings together established voices and exciting new filmmakers, with films that are funny, moving and deeply personal. We can't wait to share these stories in the heart of the city.”

Tribeca, as in its first two editions, will continue to mix indie film titles with local Portuguese cinema. Curator Rui Tendinha on the features front has selected O Dia Mais Feliz da Minha Vida , directed by Vicente Alves do Ó; António Borges Correia's Também Tu Clara ; Vindima , helmed by Luís Galvão Teles; Viagens entre Estrelas e Ondas, from filmmaker Cláudio Jordão; Tekla Taidell's 6:06 ; and Mulherzinha, a documentary by Bárbara Tinoco.

Tribeca's Portuguese indie film showcase in its third edition will move from Lisbon's Beato Innovation District to the Avenida da Liberdade, the city's tree-lined Champs-Elysees. That programming this year will include the inaugural Tribeca Night Live, a comedy, conversation, music and live performance showcase, with evenings hosted by Emmy Award-winning comedian and filmmaker W. Kamau Bell, actress Daniela Ruah and Portuguese comedian Luís Franco-Bastos. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Tribeca Festival, founded in 2003 by Robert De Niro , Jane Rosenthal and Craig Hatkoff, recently extended its partnership with the Impresa Group to stage its Portugal edition for another three years to 2028.

"Tribeca Festival Lisboa is an important part of how we're extending Tribeca's reach and connecting with audiences around the world," Rebecca Glashow, CEO of Tribeca Enterprises, said in a statement. "This partnership reflects our broader vision of bringing artists, audiences, and creative communities together in new ways, while remaining rooted in Lisbon's own creative community. articles.title: 5 Actors Rumored for DCU Roles Before James Gunn Left, And Who We Think They Might Have Played
articles.summary: The news that James Gunn and Peter Safran are out at DC Studios came as a shock to almost everyone. They were only just getting started with their lengthy plan for the future of DC movies and had put out several strong movies and shows to this point. With them out and former Marvel executive […]
articles.content:
These stars who were in talks for potential roles in James Gunn's DC Universe include some of his most consistent collaborators, actors looking for their first major superhero projects, and veterans of the genre hoping to tackle a new character. They are all interesting choices who most fans were hoping to see get involved in Gunn's world and take over some of the most notable superhero characters in the world. Of course, there's still a solid chance they could end up in future DC movies or shows, but for now we can only speculate about who they were likely going to portray.

The working relationship between Chris Pratt and James Gunn is evident. Gunn's biggest claim to fame is his Guardians of the Galaxy trilogy in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, which featured Pratt as the lead character, Peter Quill. With Gunn in charge at DC and the trilogy completed, there have been plenty of rumors of Pratt coming over. Even Pratt and Gunn have discussed this, with Pratt addressing the talk of him possibly playing Batman.

Pratt noted that Gunn had a somewhat harsh response to the idea. He said, “I sent a picture of myself with a Batman mask on. It's a little aggressive to James [Gunn]. I did it in Photoshop, and he just said ‘ha ha.' It's safe to say, I'm not going to be Batman.” That said, it would be interesting to see Pratt one day play a comic book villain, as that's outside his wheelhouse and gives him a chance to stretch his skills.

It seems like Glen Powell is in contention for every role these days. Ever since he stole scenes in Top Gun: Maverick , Powell has been everywhere from Hit Man to Twisters to Anyone But You to The Running Man . Surprisingly, the one genre we haven't seen him pop up in is superheroes, outside of a tiny role in The Dark Knight Rises before he was a star. It makes total sense that he was a name brought up for Gunn's DC vision.

As is the case with a lot of the guys discussed, people have liked the idea of Powell portraying Bruce Wayne. However, his charisma seems fit for other roles. Booster Gold was a popular idea for Powell, though he also feels like he'd be a great choice for Constantine. In fact, the idea of a Constantine project from Gunn feels like it would've been incredible and putting Powell at the forefront feels like it would've guaranteed its success.

Another name brought up often for James Gunn's DC was Jensen Ackles. The Supernatural star has been hilarious as Soldier Boy in The Boys , giving him some live-action superhero street cred. However, Ackles has a lengthy history with the genre, having voiced Jason Todd in Batman: Under the Red Hood before lending his voice to Bruce Wayne himself in a few projects, including Batman: The Long Halloween .

That has made Ackles a consistent name brought up for Batman in Gunn's planned The Brave and the Bold film. That was set to be a different take on Batman that showcases his relationship with Damian Wayne. Gunn shot down rumors of Ackles playing Batman, but there are other characters he still could've been good for. He could bring Jason Todd to life or take on heroes like Green Arrow or Booster Gold. Ackles is someone who can blend comedy with the physicality needed for these roles, so he'd fit for a lot of parts.

Similar to Glen Powell, Alan Ritchson is one of the most sought-after male actors in Hollywood these days. His lead role in Reacher is some of the best stuff on TV right now and there's no doubt that he has the physical build to play either a superhero or a villain. Of course, he's another name that has been brought up for Batman, but we think he'd actually be great as someone who opposes the Caped Crusader.

Ritchson as Slade Wilson, better known as Deathstroke, feels like an ideal fit. Again, Ritchson has the build for the role, but he can also be especially intimidating. Deathstroke would've been a perfect villain for The Brave and the Bold , though we'll likely never get that. We could also see Ritchson play Hawkman, Captain Atom, Orion, or even give us a new take on Bane. He could even go way back and play Aquaman, a role he already had early on in Smallville .

The most consistent James Gunn casting rumor has been Adria Arjona as Wonder Woman. This has been heavily discussed for months at this point and there are even people who believe she landed the role officially and was slated to make her debut in the upcoming Man of Tomorrow sequel next year. Even if that were true, that status could be up in the air with the new regime change. However, Arjona feels like a spectacular pick as Wonder Woman.

While the 2017 film about Diana Prince was well-received, people weren't raving about Gal Gadot's performance over the years. Arjona has an impressive track record already in Blink Twice, Andor , and Hit Man , among others. She has shown a knack for both drama and action, and needs a superhero redemption movie after appearing in Morbius . While people can see her as other characters, like Renee Montoya, Wonder Woman feels too perfect for Arjona to think of anything else.

Have you heard about other great James Gunn DC casting rumors? Who would you have wanted to see most? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: The Simpsons Pays Tribute to the Late Eric Bauza in Episode Featuring His Debut As Two New Characters
articles.summary: Eric Bauza photo by Monica Schipper/WireImage via Getty Images Alongside the debut of two brand new characters, The Simpsons has paid tribute to a late acting legend. The news of Eric Bauza's death in late October was sudden and unexpected, as the beloved voice actor died suddenly from hypertensive heart disease at the young age of 46. Known for his many roles as the […]
articles.content:
Shared by ToonHive on X , The Simpsons ended Season 38, Episode 7, “Dream Scenari-Moe” with a touching final tribute to Bauza just a few weeks after his passing. Eric Bauza's posthumous debut on The Simpsons saw him voice two characters, Harry Metsali — a play on the title of the beloved 1989 romantic comedy — and Mr. Fong. Despite the roles being relatively minor one-off appearances, Bauza's status in the world of voice acting made his debut on the show incredibly exciting for many fans. It might have once seemed an inevitable fusion of one of the greatest modern voice actors' talents with an iconic animated show, but due to the timing of its release, it has instead become an emotional end to Bauza's incredible career.

Eric Bauza voiced Mr. Fong and Harry Metsali in the recent ‘The Simpsons’ episode ‘Dream Scenari-Moe.’ pic.twitter.com/gM6vV5zBHW

A quick look at Eric Bauza's list of credits instantly reveals just how talented and versatile he was. His ability to both capture the essence of beloved cartoon icons to voice well-known characters and to bring all-new creations to life made him a true powerhouse in the voice acting industry, and despite his face rarely being associated with his biggest roles, he was one of the best-known voice actors in the world. Tributes to the late Eric Bauza swiftly poured in after his death, standing as a testament to the joy he brought to audiences of all ages around the world with his numerous roles in film, TV, and video games.

Considering Bauza's many impressive credits over the years, it might seem surprising to many that he didn't appear on The Simpsons sooner. With his status as one of the most prolific voice actors in the industry and The Simpsons being one of the longest-running animated shows of all time, the crossover between the two was inevitable. However, the timing of Bauza's Simpsons debut proved to be unexpectedly tragic, as the actor's sudden passing meant that his debut performance on the show also became a tribute to his incredible contributions to animation over the course of his career.

The two characters he voiced, Harry Metsali and Mr. Fong, are a good indication of just how versatile Bauza was as a voice actor. Were his name not so well-known, many viewers would never have known that the two characters shared a voice actor at all; such was the strength of Bauza's ability to adapt his voice for different roles. Though Eric Bauza being brought in to voice two characters on The Simpsons deserved to be a momentous beginning of a new collaboration, it instead has given way to a touching tribute. Considering his appearance on the show sadly proved to be all too short-lived, The Simpsons ‘ tribute to Eric Bauza is especially touching.

Do you have a favorite Eric Bauza role? Share your fondest memories of his storied career with us in the comments below.

articles.title: Beyoncé Becomes First Artist to Receive 100 Grammy Nominations
articles.summary: The superstar once again made history Monday morning when she secured a nomination in the best R&B solo performance category ahead of the February show.
articles.content:
Beyoncé is making Grammy history once again.

After securing a nomination in the best R&B solo performance category, the superstar became the first artist to achieve 100 Grammy nominations over the course of her career.

Beyoncé already holds the record as the most awarded artist in Grammys history, surpassing the late conductor Georg Solti for the all-time record of 32 wins. She first achieved the honor with a win at the 2023 Grammys in the best dance/electronic album category. Beyoncé then extended her record to 35 trophies after winning three awards during the 2025 ceremony, where she also won album of the year for Cowboy Carter , ending her streak as the most nominated female artist without a win in the album of the year category. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Music IVE, BINI, KiiiKiii, SB19, LiSA and Babymetal Score Grammy Nominations in New Asian Pop Category Music Grammys: Michael J. Her 2027 Grammy nomination follows the release of "Morning Dew (Donk)" on July 4 ahead of the 20th anniversary of her sophomore album B'Day. The track, produced by Beyoncé and Pharrell Williams, was written by Beyoncé, Williams, The-Dream and Darius Dixon.

Other nominees in the R&B solo performance category include Kehlani's "Out the Window," Victoria Monét's "Let Me," Jill Scott's "Pressha" and Tems' "What You Need."

For the 2027 Grammys , female acts make up the leading nominees with Raye topping the nominations with 11 followed by Rosalía with nine; Ella Langley, Miranda Lambert, Olivia Rodrigo and Phoebe Bridgers with seven each; and Olivia Dean with six nods, tied with Bruno Mars and Leon Thomas.

The 2027 Grammys will air on ABC, marking the first time in more than 50 years that the music awards show hasn't aired on its longtime home of CBS. The ceremony will premiere live across ABC, Disney+ and Hulu from Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles on Sunday, Feb. 7, 2027, at 7 p.m. ET / 4 p.m. PT.

And that's what the synopsis gets right into, “Yuno and Langris faced off against Zenon, who had unleashed 100% of his demonic power. Black Clover has seen the Clover Kingdom Knights needing to stop the members of the Dark Triad in order to interrupt the Advent of Qliphoth ritual before Yami and Vangeance are sacrificed, and two members of the Dark Triad and their demonic partners has been stopped thus far. articles.title: Black Cat Has Found Her New Favorite Treasure, and It's About to Lead to an X-Men Heist
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Comics Black Cat has just found her favorite new treasure, and it isn't what anyone would have expected. Felicia Hardy just met Emma Frost for the first time, and she was in love as soon as Emma activated her second mutant power. The new Black Cat series has helped expand her role in the Marvel Universe. […]
articles.content:
In Black Cat #16 (2026) by G. Willow Wilson and Andrés Genolet, Black Cat stole something from Emma Frost and then tried to fight her way out, only to see something from her dreams. Emma turned into her diamond form, and Black Cat was entranced.

Black Cat #16 saw Black Cat pulling off a new heist on the Upper West Side, where she stole a rare sapphire from an auction. The auction ended with a $5 million sale, but the sapphire mysteriously disappeared right after. After this, Black Cat began to break the fourth wall to explain how she had pulled it off. In the middle of the explanation, the sapphire began to float up in the air, and then Emma Frost was there, bringing the gem to her own hand.

After mocking Black Cat for talking to herself, Emma said that Black Cat had stolen the sapphire from her. Black Cat attacked, but she had no chance against Emma's telepathic powers. Emma asked to have a discussion about this, but Black Cat attacked again. Emma tried to use her psychic powers again, so Black Cat went for a punch, which is when Emma turned into her diamond form. That stopped Felicia on the spot as she stared at Emma in full diamond form.

This offered Black Cat a look at something she could only have dreamed about. A woman made of diamonds. As Felicia thought to herself, “What's one sapphire when there are gorgeous women made of diamonds walking the Earth?” Black Cat has spent her entire life going from one heist to another, looking for the next big score, trying to one-up the last. Facing a woman made fully of diamonds, she realized that her biggest dream was standing right in front of her. However, things went south from there.

Emma Frost took Black Cat into Felicia's own mind and gave her an ultimatum. After Black Cat promised to get her money back, Emma says she wants Black Cat to pull off a heist for her. She wants her to steal the central processing unit of an experimental generation of Sentinels that she wants to reverse-engineer to protect mutants in the future. The problem is that the X-Men have it, and they won't give it to Emma, so she wants to send in Black Cat to steal it from them.

This will open up something for Black Cat that she hasn't experienced before. Black Cat has rarely dealt with the X-Men other than crossover events like “King in Black,” and as she said here, she avoids them because they “toast people with their eye laser beams.” That is when Emma explains that she can't do this herself because of her complicated past with Cyclops. Black Cat wants nothing to do with this, but Emma says they will be enemies if she doesn't, because she doesn't like being stolen from. When Black Cat agrees, Emma tells her that she will walk through the front door to complete the heist. Also, she will have to deal with the X-Men team based in Alaska.

This is an interesting team-up for Black Cat . She is a street-level hero, and she usually pulls off heists where people like Spider-Man are around to deal with her. She is not someone who deals with people with massive superpowers. This will put her in conflict with names like Magik, Psylocke, Magneto, Kid Omega, and Beast, not to mention Cyclops. Having Black Cat try to deal with the mutants, especially a team with a psychic like Kid Omega, will force her out of her comfort zone. That is what her entire series has tried to do this entire run, and it is just getting better.

articles.title: Johnny Depp's Jack Sparrow Panicked Disney Execs: "Is He Gay?" "Is He Incredibly Drunk?"
articles.summary: In an exclusive excerpt from a new biography of the 'Ebenezer' actor, the producers of 'Pirates of the Caribbean' recall their shock at Depp's demented vision for the rogue buccaneer: "You just got to trust me."
articles.content:
In late 2000, the phone rang in the office of Dick Cook, chairman of the Walt Disney Motion Picture Group. It was Tracey Jacobs, the tenacious Hollywood agent who represented Depp and a stable of hot young actors, and her boss, the chairman of United Talent Agency, Jim Berkus. They wanted to set up a meeting between Johnny Depp and Cook.

Over the course of thirty years, Cook had risen from a ride operator at Disneyland to become head of the studio. Cook was a company man, and Johnny Depp was anything but that. He wasn't blockbuster, first-film-in-a-franchise Johnny. And in late 2000, he wasn't exactly known for starring in big-budget, family-friendly movies, either. His upcoming film was From Hell (2001), where he played opium-fueled Scotland Yard detective on the trail of Jack the Ripper. The movie grossed $74 million on a roughly $35 million budget. Respectable box office receipts, but far from what you'd call Disney numbers. Why would an actor of Depp's offbeat, gloriously demented sensibilities be interested in a studio known for its sanitized, everyman fare? It would be like unleashing Edward Scissorhands, Depp's breakthrough role, on Mickey Mouse. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Movies Johnny Depp's 'Ebenezer' Unwraps $19M to Win Weekend in Box Office Return Movies Johnny Depp's 'Ebenezer' Unearths $1.5M in Box Office Previews

On the day of the meeting at the Disney lot in Burbank, Tracey Jacobs remained in the reception area while Depp went in to meet with Cook. "He looked like just a normal guy," Cook recalled. "He wasn't dressed provocatively or anything like that. He had a couple extra rings on his fingers. But he looked great, and he was dressed nicely." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Depp launched into why he had come. Before buying his hamlet in Provence, he and Vanessa Paradis and their then almost two-year-old daughter lived in a house in a northern suburb of Paris. It was there, in the role he'd come to cherish above all others — Dad — that he'd fallen into the wonderful world of cartoons. "I've been living outside of Paris, and I have a little one," he began. "And all we do is watch Disney movies."

"Really?" said Cook. "What have you seen?"

Depp went through the list, checking off the classics of Disney animation, apparently without mentioning the edgy characters like Wile E. Coyote he'd grown to love in the Looney Tunes cartoon stable, which were the opposite of Disney's mostly wholesome fare. "Oh, we've seen Bambi and we've seen Cinderella and we've seen Snow White ," he said. "I was thinking I haven't been in any movies that are really appropriate for kids to see."

"You'd like to be a voice in one of our animated films?" Cook asked.

"I could certainly do that," Cook remembered Depp replying. "But I was thinking more of real acting. I would love to be in a Disney live-action film. Anything on the horizon?"

Cook mentally ran through the movies Disney had in development. He drew a blank. Then something struck him.

"But it's just a one- or two-page outline, kind of a description of a movie that I think we wanna do," Cook told Depp.

It was a cockamamie idea to base a movie about pirates on a Disney amusement park ride, and it was already being met with a deluge of skepticism and ridicule. "I could probably fill up a whole office full of emails that I received that this was probably the dumbest idea ever and that pirate movies, going back to Errol Flynn, were not that popular," Cook said. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

All he told Depp was the title: Pirates of the Caribbean .

" Wow, you mean the ride ?" asked Depp, visibly excited.

"Yeah, the ride," replied Cook.

Pirates of the Caribbean was one of Disneyland's most beloved attractions, along with the Monorail and the steam locomotive, which Cook had been in charge of during his days at the theme park. The film, by contrast, was still embryonic: "Just an idea," Cook said. No script, much less a director or cast. Cook didn't hold out much promise for it. Disney was preparing to release a film based on another Disneyland attraction: The Country Bears . Following a singing, one-string-guitar-strumming, harmonica-humming band of anthropomorphic bears, the movie would turn out to be a resounding flop. "Terminal inanity," film critic Roger Ebert declared. Disney would gross only $18 million against an estimated $35 million budget. But Depp wasn't thinking about box office. He was thinking about kids.

"And he said, ‘Wow, what's it about?'" Cook remembered Depp asking.

"Two pirates and a girl that's a bit of a love interest," Cook replied. "And one of the pirates is a rogue."

With that, Cook said, Depp began "moving in his seat" until he was "leaning forward," perched on the edge of his chair. What he said next was something Cook would recall more than twenty years later.

When Cook said yes, Depp lifted his arm as if brandishing a weapon. "With a sword?" blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"Yes, with a sword," Cook told him.

Depp leaned back in his seat. "Okay," he said. "I want to do it."

"You want to do what ?" Cook asked.

"I want to be the rogue pirate," replied Depp.

Cook was taken aback. "We don't have anything."

"Well, as soon as you have something, send it to me," Depp said. "'Cause I'd really like to do it."

With the meeting adjourned, Jacobs came into the office to say goodbye to Cook. But before she could utter a word, Depp told her the news. "They're gonna do a movie about the ride, Pirates of the Caribbean , and I told him I want to be in it."

Jacobs turned pale. "I think she lost all the blood in her face," said Cook.

"When I said yes to it, my agent Tracey Jacobs's head spun around like she was going to need traction," said Depp.

Before Depp threw his cutlass in the ring, Disney was envisioning Pirates as what insiders called a "straitlaced" movie, with a first-draft script so formulaic that producer Jerry Bruckheimer rejected it. The script was a "by-the-numbers pirate movie," he said. "I didn't think anybody was interested in seeing that."

But Bruckheimer saw potential. He hired screenwriters Ted Elliott and Terry Rossio (hot off of the 2001 animated comedy hit Shrek ) to add a twist to the tired old seafaring cliché.

Instead of a generic tale of pirates plundering gold, the screenwriters "came up with the idea of having the pirates turn into skeletons in the moonlight, and having to return a treasure rather than steal a treasure," Bruckheimer explained. "And I said, ‘That's unique, that's something I'd want to go see.'" To star in his cursed pirate movie, Bruckheimer agreed to give free rein to Johnny Depp. "You don't hire Johnny Depp to put him in a box," he said after meeting with the actor over what he said was a five-hour lunch with numerous bottles of very good red wine in Paris. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid4' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Disney, banking on Bruckheimer — producer of megabucks blockbusters like Top Gun and the recent live-action Disney hits The Rock , Armageddon , and Remember the Titans — agreed to pay Depp more money than the actor had ever made before: $10 million.

"I loved Captain Jack from the first moment I read the script," said Depp. Not merely because of the money, but because of the seabound maniac he could envision creating on the screen.

Depp kept quiet about his vision for Jack Sparrow. But finally, the day came when he had to unveil the character to the studio's executives. Depp found himself back on the Disney lot in Burbank, for a hair and makeup test on Stage 2. Soon, the phone rang in the office of Dick Cook. It was a call from the set. "Oh my gosh," his people told him. "You wouldn't believe what Johnny has done."

"He's capped all of his teeth gold, and he has diamonds in most of them, and he has probably spent two days in a dentist chair getting all of this work done. It's crazy. It's too much."

Cook tried to get Jerry Bruckheimer and the film's director, Gore Verbinski, to speak to Depp, but they were both too savvy to accept the assignment. "Neither one of them wanted to have this conversation with him, because he was so happy with his teeth," Cook recalled. "And neither wanted to start off the production with an issue with Johnny."

Cook asked to see photos from the hair and makeup test. Sure enough, every tooth in Depp's famous smile was covered in gold. Hanging the photos on the wall of a screening room, he asked Depp to meet him there the next morning. "Immediately I got calls from Tracey Jacobs and his attorney and everyone else wanting to come to the meeting," said Cook. "I said, ‘No, this is not necessary. It's just going to be the two of us.' I didn't want an audience." Depp knew what was up. "Is this about my teeth?" he asked immediately upon arriving. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid5' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"Let's talk about it," Cook said. He motioned to the photos on his wall. "So what are you looking at?"

"I'm looking at my mouth," said Depp.

Cook replied, "We need to be looking at your eyes. That's where we need to focus."

Depp nodded. "Yep, you're right. Okay. Do you have a mirror?"

Cook borrowed a compact makeup mirror from a receptionist outside his office and spent the next hour with Depp "marking the teeth that we had to take out the gold. There was one tooth that was on the side, and it had a little diamond in it. Johnny said, ‘Can I keep that one?' And I said, ‘Yeah, you can keep that one.' And he did."

But Depp wasn't finished with Captain Jack. Back in the hair and makeup chair [MS2] , his longtime makeup wizard, Ve Neill, began to apply the final touches to the rum- and sun-addled pirate Depp envisioned. First, she went to work on his face. Around the eyes, she applied raccoon-like rings of kohl. The more crazed, the better , implored Depp. There were beads and scarves and rotting dreadlocks and clothes designed to look like they had been stolen. Still, the actor wanted more. "More and more and more and more and more!" he said.

Finally, the time came for Depp to present his vision of Jack Sparrow to a gathering of Disney executives. Those in attendance that day remembered it as nothing short of a shock. First the gold-toothed smile. Then the slurred faux-British accent. ( What the fuck is he saying? ) Then the raccoon-eyed face. ( Absolutely unrecognizable! ) Then the dreadlocks, and the swishy scarves, and the wobbly walk. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid6' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The executives looked back and forth at each other as if to say, What the fuck? Where's the actor who cost us $10 million? This is going to be a disaster!

The phone calls ricocheted between the alarmed executives:

"What's going on? Is he just mentally just . . . gone ?"

To that last one, Depp responded, "I'm sorry, didn't you know all of my characters are gay?"

The furor rose to the very top of the studio. Before long, Depp heard that Michael Eisner, Disney's chairman and CEO, was in a full-blown panic. "Depp is ruining the film!" he reportedly shrieked. "We're going to have to subtitle it! Nobody can understand what he's saying! What is he doing ?"

Depp had been around Hollywood long enough to know what the suits were thinking. "I understood their worries," he said, "because the film they released just prior to that was the Country Bear Jamboree [ The Country Bears ]." Disney couldn't afford another costly flop—especially another one based on a theme park attraction. And at that time, Depp hardly seemed like a bankable star. "In terms of Hollywood and the business and films that make money at the box office and all that, I essentially had a career of about 20 years of failures, in their eyes," he said. " Ed Wood " — the 1994 comedy/drama released by Disney's Touchstone subsidiary in which he played the inept cross-dressing B-movie director — "was a flop to them," as were "any of the other stranger films." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid7' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Fed up with the pushback and hand-wringing, Depp decided to throw down the gauntlet. "I put it to them that they were welcome to fire me and replace me if they wanted to," he said. "‘Cause I wasn't going to change what I built because I believed in it. I believed in the character wholeheartedly. I felt very comfortable with him, and I felt I was on to something."

Disney's executives tasked Nina Jacobson, president of the Walt Disney Motion Picture Group, with calling Depp. Jacobson had grown up in Los Angeles going to Disneyland in Anaheim, and she already knew that Pirates would be an uphill battle — even before the arrival of Johnny Depp. "Nobody had made a successful pirate movie," she said. "Plus, we had just fallen on our face with our first go at a ride turned into a movie. People thought we were really dumb in making Pirates of the Caribbean . There was zero buzz."

Now the leading man had gone off the rails.

"What's up?" she recalled asking Depp. "What are you doing?"

Depp's response was simple. "You got to trust me," he told her. "You just got to trust me."

Depp was asking Disney to trust him with a $140 million bet on a vision that came to him in a broiling sauna, a vision that turned a flesh-and-blood pirate into a full-blown cartoon. From a business perspective, it made no sense. But it was too late to make a change. To replace the leading man in the middle of production would detonate a stink bomb that would put the industry doomsayers into overdrive — a fallout worse than the Country Bears debacle. Disney had no choice. And soon their baby, Pirates of the Caribbean , a lark born of a Disneyland ride and entrusted to one of Hollywood's most eccentric actors, would be presented to the world. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid8' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

articles.content:
Among the 2027 Grammy Awards newest categories is the highly discussed best Asian pop performance category. The inaugural class of the category spans three countries and includes two artists from southeast Asia , a region often overlooked in the Asian pop conversation.

Coachella breakouts BINI , an eight-member girl group, and 2027 Coachella performers SB19, a five-member boy group, are both nominated, representing the rapidly-growing music industry in the Philippines. BINI has been nominated for their song “Unang Kilig” and SB19 has been nominated for their song “Visa.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Music Grammys: Michael J. Fox, Tim Curry, 'Wicked: For Good,' 'The Pitt' Among Hollywood Nominees Music Dolly Parton Lands Three Posthumous Grammy Nominations

Starships Entertainment's two biggest acts, girl groups IVE and KiiiKiii, will represent the K-pop industry in the category. IVE, consistently one of Korea's biggest domestic acts since their 2021 debut, has been nominated for the song “Bang Bang.” The catchy track, released as the beginning of the year, was a quick hit for the group. KiiiKiii, who debuted in 2025 with extreme promise, has been nominated for the dance-pop hit, “404 (New Era).” The track cemented the group's signature sound.

K-pop superstars BTS announced earlier this year that they'd be boycotting Grammy submissions due to the category, with many other K-pop acts quietly following suit. Japan, with two nominations, had a smaller than expected presence, given the country has the world's second-largest music industry. articles.content:
Morocco's fourth biggest city of Marrakech has been in the spotlight domestically in recent weeks after its longtime mayor Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri was appointed the country's first female prime minister at the end of September.

The Red City, so called because of the ochre-coloured walls of its historic center, will be back in the news this week as its Marrakech International Film Festival gets underway.

The 23rd edition opens Friday (Nov 20) with a gala screening of Jesse Eisenberg's New Jersey-set comedy The Debut with Julianne Moore and Paul Giamatti. Related Stories News Jeff Goldblum, John Turturro & Younès Mégri To Be Honored At Marrakech; Rian Johnson & James Gray Set For Conversations Festivals Antonin Baudry & Simon Abkarian Talk French Box Office Hit 'De Gaulle': "The National Icon Did Not Exist In 1940"

"I love Jesse Eisenberg both as an actor and a filmmaker. This film is just a great and clever comedy in which we also get to Julianne Moore as we never see her," says Artistic Director Remi Bonhomme, alluding to the actress's role as a housewife who auditions for a musical and is cast in a supporting role. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Watch on Deadline if ( !window.pmc.harmony?.isEventAdScheduledTime() ) { pmcCnx.cmd.push(function() { pmcCnx({ settings: { plugins: { pmcAtlasMG: { iabPlcmt: 2, } } }, playerId: '32fe25c4-79aa-406a-af44-69b41e969e71', playlistId: '0199e506-e642-7728-8264-463efe71337b', }).render("connatix_contextual_player_div"); }); } else { // This should only be get called when page cache is not cleared and it's event time. window.pmc.harmony?.switchToHarmonyPlayer(); }

In the backdrop, preparations for the festival have unfolded amid unsettled times for the MENA region in the wake of the military campaign launched by the U.S. and Israel against Iran's Islamic Regime government in February.

Saudi Arabia is also dealing with the resurgence of Iran-backed Houthi forces in neighboring Yemen, who have been firing drones and missiles at its cities, cementing the cancelation of a number of events including the Red Sea International Film Festival in Jeddah.

"We're not in the Gulf, so we're not affected directly but of course we are indirectly," says Bonhomme citing rising costs linked to the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. "The cancellation of the Red Sea was sad news, and I really express my solidarity with them."

Jesse Eisenberg's and his cast will not be travelling to Marrakech for The Debut gala screening but there will be plenty of glitz and glamor as the starry jury headed by Marion Cotillard is presented on stage. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The Oscar-winning French actress will be joined by actors Claes Bang, Vicky Krieps, Emma Mackey as well as actor-filmmaker Gilles Lellouche and directors Kaouther Ben Hania, Andrew Haigh, Ramata-Toulaye Sy and Saïd Hamich Benlarbi.

The Debut will kick off a nine-day program showcasing 76 films from close to 40 territories. Further gala highlights include Luca Guadagnino's Sam Altman biopic Artificial ; Noah Segan's The Only Living Pickpocket In New York and James Gray's Paper Tiger .

" Artificial has only shown in New York and London, so very few people have seen it," says Bonhomme. "Luca is very close to the festival, while its MENA distributor Gianluca Chakra at Front Row is crazy about the film and was keen to show it here."

The Only Living Pickpocket In New York will be accompanied by its star John Turturro, who is one of the festival's honourees this year alongside Jeff Goldblum and Moroccan actor, songwriter and performer Younès Megri

"This film is 3,000% John Turturro," says Bonhomme of the drama set and shot in contemporary working-class neighbourhoods across New York as well as the subway. "It was a real pleasure to plunge into his films in preparation for the tribute… when you see his career, there's certain kind of freedom and also a curiosity.

The gala lineup is also hosting two big world premieres for the MENA region: Omar Hilal's His Weakest Creatures and Fellipe Barbosa's Leila et La Nuit.

Brazilian director Fellipe Barbosa's Leila et La Nuit takes its cue from the death of Moroccan photographer Leila Alaoui who was killed while on assignment in Burkina Faso in 2016.

Inspired by the book ‘Off To Ouaga' by her father, it follows her family as they first get news that something has happened with the cast featuring Roschdy Zem, Marina Foïs, Sayyid El Alami and Oulaya Amamra.

"I absolutely wanted this film to premiere in Marrakesh. They shot the film in Marrakesh. The family comes from Marrakesh. I also personally knew Leila," says Bonhomme.

"We had long discussions with the sales agent Lucky Number and Fellipe to make it happen. It's going to be a very emotional night with the family also attending,” he adds.

His Weakest Creatures is the latest film from Egypt's Hilal after breakout hit Voy! Voy! Voy! and brings Egyptian stars Ahmed Helmy and Hend Sabry together on the big screen for the first time.

Helmy will play a principled zoologist working in Cairo's historical Giza Zoo, struggling to uphold his values amid dwindling resources and quiet institutional decay, when a wealthy visitor offers to "adopt" surplus animals.

“This film is a much higher budget film than Voy! Voy! Voy! with a lot of ambition. It's a comedy, thriller and adventure film too. There's strong anticipation across the region,” says Bonhomme.

Cotillard and her jury will decide the winners of festival's main competition featuring 14 first and second films.

Recent recipients of its top Étoile d'Or prize for best film have included Erige Sehiri's Promised Sky (2025), Scandar Copti's Happy Holidays (2024), and Asmae El Moudir's The Mother of all Lies (2023).

As was the case last year, Bonhomme suggests that many of the contenders chime with the recent rise of Gen Z movements across the world questioning the current status quo.

"I'm impressed by the maturity of these filmmakers. The accountability they ask for from the previous generation," he says, pointing to Marie-Clémentine Dusabejambo's Ben'imana, exploring the legacy of the 1994 Rwandan genocide, as an example. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-articleX","mid-article","btf","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() ; });

" Ben'imana is a film going back to explore the genocide by someone who lived the genocide as a child… several of the films are going back to the previous generations or are even historical films," he continues

On the latter, he cites Moroccan Italian director Yassine Marco Marroccu's Alkebulan . Inspired by his grandfather's diaries, it follows the adventures of an Italian émigré who sets off on a mission to recover the cargo of a merchant ship which sinks off the Sahara's Atlantic coast, with the story running from the 1930s to the 1960s.

"For a long time, first and second films were coming-of-age film where filmmakers would go back to their childhood or teenage years," says Bonhomme. "We still have these but I'm seeing have more and more adult stories.

He points to films such as Auguste Bernard Kouemo Yanghu's House of the Wind and Rami Kodeih's Furies as further example of this.

" House of the Wind tackles question of migration through the lens of the people left behind. It's a fresh approach,” he notes.

In programming hat-trick, three titles arrive in Marrakech's competition having won the best first film prize at an A-list festivals.

Ben'imana , world premiered in Cannes Un Certain Regard and won the Caméra d'Or; House of the Wind debuted in Venice's Orizzonti, winning its Jury Prize, and the Lion of the Future Luigi De Laurentiis, while Abdallah Al-Khatib's In Chronicles from the Siege , about Palestinian civilians trapped in a war zone, was feted with the Berlinale's Best First Feature Award.

"Awarding the best first film in Cannes, Berlin or Venice is always the hardest task… the fact the jurors went for Arab and African films says a lot about what going on with filmmaking in these regions," says Bonhomme.

Three films world premiere in competition: Alkebulan , Rani Massalha and Salem Massalha's Cairo Shadows, set within in the Copt community in Cairo, and Iranian Norwegian director Farzad Samsami's Waves of Silence.

"It's kind of a moral drama shot like a western in a small town by the sea,” says Bonhomme. “It's a film dealing with the question of migrants, but it's also a film reuniting three one of the best actors in Morocco, for me, Amine Ennaji, Nisrin Erradi and Younes Bouab.

" Cairo Shadows is a gripping thriller, which also features a very great discovery of a young Egyptian actor called Hassan Malek," he continues, referring to the rising young star who is the brother of exstablised star Ahmed Malek.

"It's set in the Copt community. It's funny because James Gray is attending the festival this year and the film reminds of me his first film Little Odessa and the questions it raises about what it means to belongs to a tightknit community and whether its possible to ever leave it."

Beyond the Competition and Gala screenings competition, the festival will showcase a raft of seasons frontrunners in the world cinema-focused sidebar Horizons including Fjord , All Of Sudden , Everytime and Fatherland .

Bonhomme reveals that a move to shift the festival dates forward by one week this year was prompted in part by a desire to interconnect more seamlessly with the awards season.

"We want to position the festival at the beginning of the Oscar campaign and to have all these films and names here as it kicks off," he says, noting these dates ties in nicely with the Gotham Awards in New York on November 30.

articles.title: At Cairo Film Festival, Arab Women Filmmakers Ask: ‘What Freedom Do We Have to Tell Our Own Stories?’
articles.summary: Arab women filmmakers are making their mark on the international stage, with their films earning recognition at major festivals and reaching audiences around the world. But as their visibility grows, questions remain about the opportunities available to them beyond the festival circuit, from securing financing and distribution to building sustainable careers. Those questions are at […]
articles.content:
Arab women filmmakers are making their mark on the international stage, with their films earning recognition at major festivals and reaching audiences around the world. But as their visibility grows, questions remain about the opportunities available to them beyond the festival circuit, from securing financing and distribution to building sustainable careers.

Those questions are at the center of a discussion on Arab women directors and the mainstream film industry at the 47th Cairo Intl. Film Festival . For Palestinian director Laila Abbas , Egyptian producer Khouloud Sa'd and Egyptian filmmaker Amal Ramsis, the conversation goes beyond representation to examine the structures shaping which films get made, whose stories reach audiences and what it takes to sustain a career in the region. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Taika Waititi Slams ‘Klara and the Sun’ Critics as ‘Irrelevant,’ ‘Sad Lost Souls’ and Says He Hasn’t ‘Read a Review’ in 15 Years: 'But I Do Listen to the People’

"As Arab women filmmakers, we exist," Ramsis tells Variety . "But which kind of stories can we tell? What freedom do we have to tell our own stories?"

Ramsis challenges the idea that success should be measured primarily by recognition at major European festivals. While acknowledging their importance, she argues that filmmakers need alternative distribution networks and more direct connections with audiences.

"We don't lack films from women directors in the international festivals. We are there," she says, arguing that the conversation should focus less on numbers and more on creative freedom.

That freedom, she maintains, remains constrained by expectations about the stories Arab women should tell. "As an Arab woman filmmaker, you should talk about women as victims, you should talk about the veil," she says. "Maybe sometimes that's not the way we want to talk about our issues." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Abbas, whose debut feature " Thank You for Banking With Us! " explores gender discrimination in inheritance laws through humor, has encountered similar expectations when seeking financing.

"Sometimes we think that Europeans want to see a certain type of film coming from the Middle East," Abbas explains. "If you're outside of trauma, war, conflict, then they would not be very interested."

Yet she cautions that the reality is more complicated. Films addressing politically sensitive subjects can also deter potential backers, leaving filmmakers to navigate different expectations depending on the project.

Abbas also challenges the assumption that Arab women directors necessarily face the same barriers as their counterparts elsewhere. Pointing to the prominence of female filmmakers in Palestinian cinema, including Cherien Dabis , director of "All That's Left of You," and Annemarie Jacir , director of "Palestine 36," she argues that the region's particular circumstances deserve greater attention.

"When I look at the Arab world and I see all the initiatives revolving around cinema, whether it's labs or festivals, I see a good presence for women," she says. "I've never really felt that I'm discriminated against when it comes to a story that I've written because I'm a woman."

For Egyptian producer Sa'd, whose credits include Mohammed Hammad's independently financed El Gouna winner "Safe Exit," the growing number of women filmmakers is an encouraging development.

"There are many voices from Egyptian and Arab women in the industry now, and they have a variety of subjects and issues they want to address," she says. "They're getting more prominence, and I think it's very useful for the industry."

Yet greater visibility, she cautions, does not necessarily mean greater access to audiences. "We have many women directors. They have the quality, the topics and subjects, but distribution remains a very big problem," she explains.

Sa'd points to "Safe Exit" and "Withered Green" as examples of independent productions that offer "another vision" for an Egyptian industry she says has struggled with production and distribution in recent years. She sees self-financing as one way to create opportunities for emerging filmmakers outside of traditional production structures. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

But that independence comes at a cost. "The journey of these films is very, very long," she laments, noting that self-financed projects can take five or six years to complete. "More funding would make the process shorter and easier. There's a direct relationship between money and time it takes to complete projects."

Sa'd also calls for closer cooperation between producers, distributors and sales agents to help films reach wider audiences. "We should have even more cooperation between the producers, distributors and sales agents," she says, emphasizing the importance of trust between industry players. "The producer and distributor are like a marriage."

Financing remains another concern. Abbas welcomes the proliferation of development labs across the region, which give emerging filmmakers opportunities to refine scripts, build networks and meet potential collaborators.

"These places where you actually meet people, where you make connections, where you hear feedback on your script from different people, from different places around the world," she says. "These insights are very, very important."

But she argues that the funding available to turn those projects into films remains woefully insufficient. "We're all relying on three, four funds in the region," she says, pointing to the absence of national film funds in many countries. Without financial backing from home, Arab filmmakers can find themselves at a disadvantage when approaching international co-producers. "That's not sustainable," she adds.

Ramsis identifies another gap in the industry's support structures: the difficulty of maintaining a career beyond the first or second feature. "Once you make your third film and you haven't become famous, very famous, it's very difficult to continue in this industry," she says, noting that many funding initiatives prioritize emerging talent.

Ramsis is a founder of the Between Women Filmmakers' Caravan initiative, which was established in 2008. Through this project, Ramsis has sought to build alternatives, organizing screenings, workshops and collaborative production opportunities for women across the Arab world and Latin America.

"It's not a project on women, it's a project made by women," she explains. "One of our main goals is to create this big networking between women filmmakers, to exchange experiences and to talk about our challenges in the industry." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

For Abbas, the way forward also requires established filmmakers to help create opportunities for the next generation. "Reach back to filmmakers, create a fund for new talent. Do something," she urges.

The challenge, the industry veterans agree, is not simply getting Arab women filmmakers into the mainstream, but ensuring they have the creative freedom, resources and industry support to remain there.

articles.content:
Ben McKenzie will moderate the premiere Q&A for Netflix's " The Altruists " with stars Julia Garner and Anthony Boyle and showrunner Graham Moore on Nov. 19 in New York, the same day the series premieres on the streamer.

Known now as an anti-crypto activist as well as an actor, McKenzie followed his successful runs on television shows like “The O.C.” and “Gotham” by writing the New York Times bestselling novel "Easy Money," which compares cryptocurrency to the devastation of historic financial crashes. He then wrote, directed and produced the 2025 documentary "Everyone is Lying to You for Money," which chronicles his investigation into the crypto industry for the book, and includes a one-on-one sitdown interview with Sam Bankman-Fried, whose story is the subject of “The Altruists” (he's played by Boyle). blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Taika Waititi Slams ‘Klara and the Sun’ Critics as ‘Irrelevant,’ ‘Sad Lost Souls’ and Says He Hasn’t ‘Read a Review’ in 15 Years: 'But I Do Listen to the People’

"Everyone is Lying to You for Money" premiered at SXSW London in June 2025 and played at several other festivals. Independent distributor The Forge acquired distribution and sales rights in March 2025, and the film had a limited theatrical run starting in April 2026. Variety 's Owen Gleiberman described the film as "lively, knife-sharp, impeccably researched" and said it "answers every conceivable question you've ever had about crypto.” The film is still looking for a streaming partner, but is currently available for rent via Eventive, C5.now, Amazon and Kanopy in the U.S.

"The Altruists" stars Boyle and Garner as Caroline Ellison. Premiering Nov. 19, the Netflix limited series follows the crypto Bonnie and Clyde through the rise and fall of FTX, the Bankman-Fried-founded cryptocurrency exchange and hedge fund. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

At his peak, Bankman-Fried was the 41st-richest American on the Forbes 400 list. FTX was forced to go bankrupt in November 2022 after evidence of fraud surfaced. Bankman-Fried was arrested in December 2022 and has since been sentenced to 25 years in prison. Ellison was sentenced to 24 months in prison and served 14 before being released in January.
